choices.content: Corresponding sides of homothetic figures are not necessarily parallel.
The lines joining corresponding points of homothetic figures do not necessarily intersect at a single point.

question.prompt: Which of the following statements about homothety is correct?

solutions.explanation: Homothety is a special type of similarity: the lines joining corresponding points intersect at a single point (the center of homothety), and corresponding sides are parallel. Therefore, homothetic figures are always similar, but the converse is not necessarily true.
solutions.title: Use the defining properties of homothety
